title: Text can be anything
idea: The text inside the quotes can be words, whole sentences, or symbols — the computer shows it exactly.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

print("Hello, world!")
exercises.explanation: Everything inside the quotes is shown exactly, including the comma and the !

exercises.prompt: You can put a whole sentence inside one print.
exercises.explanation: One pair of quotes can hold a single word or a long sentence — all shown exactly.
It's inside quotes, so it's just text. The computer shows 3 + 4, it does NOT do the math. (Numbers without quotes behave differently — more soon.)

exercises.prompt: Build an instruction that shows: I love coding
exercises.explanation: The whole phrase with its spaces lives in one pair of quotes.
Symbols are text too. The computer shows exactly what's in the quotes: ***

exercises.prompt:
Complete this to show the sentence: See you soon

print(____)
exercises.explanation: The full sentence goes inside one pair of quotes.
Anything inside the quotes is shown exactly — even if it looks like a number. So print("7") shows 7.

exercises.prompt:
Which instruction shows this exact line?

Welcome to Dailo
exercises.explanation: The whole line, as one piece of text, inside one pair of quotes.
Digits and symbols are fine as text. This shows 100%

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

print("Line one")
exercises.explanation: Exactly the text in the quotes: Line one.
